decision.consumerEightFiles: No confirmed blocking defect found in the reviewed implementation; this is source review only.
decision.releaseAggregate: Change requested for premature overall passed flag.

facts: Each graph has a distinct project and cache under a new temporary root outside the checkout.
Direct references use exact [version] constraints and conditional symbols select only the intended facade imports.
Derived owned subclosure counts are 10,10,5,6,6,17; combined includes all seventeen identities.
The destination is first validated against the full manifest/release record; per-graph assets libraries must equal the selected owned IDs/versions.
Every actually restored owned nupkg is hashed against the manifest, and the shipped MSBuild task checks exact owned dependency edges.
Final destination readback verifies immutable bytes. This claims the owned NativeWeave closure; external dependencies retain normal NuGet locks and are not mislabeled as owned packages.

checks.area: Native identity and ordinary managed edits
facts: Output records are checked against facade ID/version, engine, RID, source path and exact native SHA; record sets exclude undeclared engines.
Combined ordinary Entity/DTO/Handler source is added after both restores, restore sources are cleared, and build/publish use --no-restore.
The typed table insert/materialization and added HTTP handler are actually invoked, then JIT/AOT native hashes must match pre-edit identities.

checks.area: Actual AOT execution and domain operations
checks.assessment: Source path implemented; formal runtime execution still pending
facts: Each graph calls dotnet publish with PublishAot, audits the ELF, requires absence of the managed consumer DLL and starts the produced executable with --require-aot.
The application checks RuntimeFeature.IsDynamicCodeSupported=false and terminal expected checks; real PostgreSQL requires explicit environment configuration.
Server cases issue actual TLS HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2, bounded gRPC and MCP calls; database and server retirement checks precede terminal success receipt.

checks.area: Negative cases invoke real code paths
checks.assessment: Source path implemented; formal negative execution still pending
facts: ABI major 99 uses the actual provider-specific exported bootstrap and fresh process, before database creation.
Missing output record and native-byte tampering run fresh AOT processes and require the actual loader error; originals are restored and identities rechecked.
Direct package override variants restore separate caches and must reach the shipped closure task hard error; missing leaf is exercised at NuGet restore.

Valid control, omitted SDK-selected native item, unsupported RID and tampered native content call the packaged PackageClosure task against the actual domain closure/assets, with specific expected errors.

checks.assessment: Receipt identity and process contract implemented; see separate aggregate-result finding
facts: The callback starts a separate consumer process, which starts fresh application processes for the combined previous graph and both providers.
Publisher and rollback validate passed/rid/source_commit/full package hash map, and rollback rejects active process and incomplete/wrong-source closures.
Previous smoke accurately omits candidate AOT/negative acceptance; actual provider operations and owner cleanup still run.

checks.assessment: Interface statically aligned with separately hashed CI snapshot
facts: CI mounts only the AOT bundle, standalone verifier and result directory into the pinned Noble runtime image; no checkout/cache/toolchain is mounted.
Python is installed for the verifier; absence checks cover dotnet, Cargo, Rust and compiler tools.
Runtime verifier requires all six graphs/provider rows, bound executable inventory/ELF audit, actual --require-aot process checks, and before/after file hashes.
Formal OCI execution is not inferred from environment assertions or static source.

checks.assessment: Consistent with implementation and pending formal evidence
facts: Guide explains local-only seventeen-package pair, exact split versions, six graphs, ordinary edit workflow, runtime transfer and receipt boundaries.
No public domain release/signature acceptance, multiday soak, historical benchmark identity transfer or unexecuted platform claim is made.

findings.title: Release aggregate reports passed before the complete sequence finishes
findings.observation: record() appends only a passed case and immediately serializes overall passed=all(recorded cases). Therefore the first controlled partial-publication case already leaves result.json and evidence/result.json with passed=true. A later consumer/AOT/rollback exception or interruption does not clear it; no terminal-complete field is present.
findings.impact: A retained aggregate file can assert success while later required B24 steps did not finish. The actual subprocess/CI still fails and publication callbacks still enforce their receipts; this finding concerns truthful aggregate evidence, not a bypass of catalog publication.
findings.recommendedChange: Keep aggregate passed=false while running and on failure/interruption; set true only after all existing steps and final evidence writes succeed. Preserve successful case details. No additional acceptance case or gate is requested.
findings.verificationMethod: Read-only source control-flow inspection; no synthetic test, application or consumer execution.

supplementalDevelopmentPreflight.claim: Read existing bounded development receipt and verified source identity only; this reviewer did not execute its commands.

limitations: Static review does not establish formal SDK image, runtime-only image, PostgreSQL, AOT or negative-case execution success.
CI files were uncommitted working-tree snapshots at input binding; future CI delta must be separately bound.
The finding is in the previously integrated release controller, not the new consumer eight-file commit.
